q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution

Q2 FY2027 earnings will be reported in late August 2026 (approximately 2 weeks from the current date of 2026-08-15). The forward guidance will be announced at that time.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 guidance was $91.0B (±2%), which implies a range of $89.18B to $92.82B. They reported actual Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B on May 20, 2026.

The guidance of $91.0B for Q2 represents sequential growth from Q1's $81.6B actual — an increase of approximately 11.6%. This is a reasonable sequential growth rate for NVIDIA given:
- Strong demand for AI chips and data center solutions
- Historical quarterly growth patterns in high-demand environments
- The guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center compute revenue, which is a conservative assumption

Analyst consensus sits at $91.8B with a range of $90.3B to $96.7B. The current guidance of $91.0B is slightly below the median analyst estimate, which is typical for NVIDIA's historically conservative guidance patterns.

**Most likely outcome:** NVIDIA will provide guidance very close to the $91.0B they've already stated, potentially within ±2% ($89.18B to $92.82B), with the actual outcome likely in the $90.5B to $91.5B range.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Unexpected weakness in data center demand
- Accelerated export restrictions to China beyond current assumptions
- Supply chain disruptions
- Stronger-than-expected competition in AI accelerators
- Macroeconomic softening affecting enterprise spending
- Execution issues in new product launches
- Market share losses to competing solutions

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected data center bookings and pull-through
- Acceleration in AI adoption across new verticals/geographies
- Higher ASPs (average selling prices) for premium configurations
- Partial relaxation of China export restrictions leading to incremental revenue
- Customer demand exceeding supply (backlog extension)
- Success of new product lines beyond base case assumptions
- Beats on Q1 actual driving upward guidance revisions

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 guidance was $91.0B (±2%)
- Q1 FY2027 actual was $81.6B
- Analyst consensus for Q2 FY2027 is $91.8B (range: $90.3B to $96.7B)
- Year-over-year growth in Q1 was 85%

The guidance range provided ($99.5B to $115.5B) appears to represent a much higher expectation than either NVIDIA's stated guidance or analyst consensus. This suggests the question may be testing whether a significant upside surprise occurs.

## Reasoning on the distribution

Given that:
1. NVIDIA already provided formal guidance of $91.0B (±2%) for Q2
2. Analyst consensus is $91.8B, centered around the guidance
3. The range in the question ($99.5B-$115.5B) is substantially higher than current expectations
4. We are only 2 weeks from the earnings release, leaving minimal time for major guidance revisions

The most likely outcome clusters around $90-92B. The probability of guidance reaching the lower end of the stated range ($99.5B) would require a significant upward surprise that appears inconsistent with current information. The upper end ($115.5B) would represent an 27% increase from guidance — an extreme outlier requiring multiple positive surprises.

A reasonable distribution would:
- Center near the stated guidance of $91.0B
- Have some upside bias toward analyst consensus at $91.8B
- Assign low but non-negligible probability to the $99.5B+ range (potential surprise)
- Assign very low probability to extreme highs above $110B

**My estimate:**
- 10th percentile (lower): Around $89.5B (below guidance floor, unlikely bear case)
- 50th percentile (median): Around $91.0-91.5B (at/near stated guidance)
- 90th percentile (upper): Around $95.0B (analyst high end, significant beat scenario)

Low (10th percentile): 89500000000
Median (50th percentile): 91200000000
High (90th percentile): 95000000000

NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, as of their Q1 FY2027 earnings release on May 20, 2026, is an expected revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). This guidance does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

Analysts' consensus for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.8 billion, with a range of $90.3 billion to $96.7 billion [tickerleague.com](https://tickerleague.com/companies/NVDA/estimates). NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 revenue, reported on May 20, 2026, was $81.6 billion, up 85% year-over-year [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), exceeding Wall Street estimates [barchart.com](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3449043/what-to-expect-from-nvidia-s-q2-2027-earnings-report).
